post_text:
Day 6/30 — System.Threading.Channels (.NET & C#)

Saw a worker service starving the thread pool last week because BlockingCollection.Take() blocks OS threads under low load.

• **Thread Starvation:** BlockingCollection puts worker threads to sleep on Monitor primitives, hurting scalability during traffic spikes.

• **Lock-Free Mechanics:** Channel<T> relies on Interlocked state machines, streaming via ValueTasks with near-zero Gen0 allocations.

• **Backpressure Control:** BoundedChannelOptions lets you drop oldest, drop newest, or apply backpressure without blocking execution threads.

Watch out: Always call Writer.Complete() or Readers waiting on ReadAllAsync will hang indefinitely.

Are you still using BlockingCollection in background services?
